findings.title: Public group members page now shows only first 50 members with no pagination
findings.body: The public group members route (`group-members`) now calls `model.findMembers()` which uses the model's default `limit` of 50. The template iterates over `members` without any pagination controls, so for any group with more than 50 members, only the first 50 are displayed and there is no way to see the rest. Previously, non-automatic groups showed all members. This is a functional regression for public group pages.

findings.title: totalPages calculation is off-by-one when user_count is divisible by limit
findings.body: The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2. This causes `showingLast` to remain false on the final page, so the next button stays enabled and clicking it does nothing (offset is clamped to user_count). The UI shows an extra non-existent page.

findings.title: Admin group creation ignores alias_level parameter
findings.body: The `create` action only sets `name` and `visible` from params; it does not set `alias_level`. The frontend form always displays the alias level combo box (even for new groups), but any value selected by the user is silently discarded during creation. The group will be created with the default alias level instead of the chosen one.

findings.title: No upper bound on limit parameter for public members endpoint
findings.body: The `members` action uses `(params[:limit] || 50).to_i` without validating that the provided limit is reasonable. A client could request `limit=1000000` or higher, causing the server to load and serialize a huge number of records, potentially degrading performance or exhausting memory. A maximum value (e.g., 200) should be enforced.
